B03C069.summary: Sudeva, a Brahmana searching for Nala, finds Damayanti in the household of the queen-mother and identifies her by a mark on her forehead. The queen-mother recognizes her as a sister's daughter, and Damayanti is sent home to Vidarbha. There she asks her father to have Nala sought, and Brahmanas are dispatched across the lands to find him.

scenes.B03C069S01: Sudeva identifies Damayanti by the mark on her brow, her kin recognize her, and she sends searchers out to find Nala.

shots.B03C069S01H01: Sudeva tells the queen-mother who the woman is: Bhima's daughter and Nala's wife, who went off unseen with him after Nala lost his kingdom at dice.
shots.B03C069S01H02: The dust is washed from the mark, the queen-mother recognizes her niece, Damayanti is sent home to Vidarbha, and she asks that Nala be searched for.
shots.B03C069S01H03: The Brahmanas set out through cities, hermitages and cowherd lands, repeating Damayanti's message wherever they go.

B03C070.summary: Parnada, a Brahmana, returns from Ayodhya with the report that King Rituparna gave no answer to Damayanti's message, though his charioteer Vahuka spoke to him kindly. Damayanti then arranges a trick: she sends Sudeva to Rituparna with word of a second swayamvara the next day, hoping to bring Nala to Vidarbha. She keeps the plan from her father.

scenes.B03C070S01: Parnada reports the reply he received in Ayodhya, and Damayanti sends Sudeva to Rituparna with a false announcement of a swayamvara.

shots.B03C070S01H01: Parnada says Rituparna ignored the message, but the charioteer Vahuka answered with sympathetic words about the patience a faithful wife should show.
shots.B03C070S01H02: Damayanti asks her mother to keep the plan from Bhima, sends Sudeva off with the false swayamvara news, and rewards Parnada with wealth and a promise of more.

B03C071.summary: Rituparna decides to reach Vidarbha in a single day for the swayamvara, and Nala, now serving as the charioteer Vahuka, is torn by doubt about whether Damayanti's plan is genuine. Vahuka selects and yokes the horses, and the car rises swiftly into the air. Varshneya, Nala's former charioteer, notices Vahuka's skill and begins to suspect that he is Nala.

scenes.B03C071S01: Rituparna sets out for the swayamvara, Nala weighs his doubts while driving the horses, and Varshneya begins to suspect Vahuka's true identity.

shots.B03C071S01H01: Nala, disguised as Vahuka, doubts Damayanti's motive yet agrees to go; he yokes the horses, the car rushes off, and Varshneya, judging Vahuka's skill, begins to suspect he is Nala.

B03C072.summary: On the road Rituparna's upper garment falls, and to show his skill he counts the leaves and fruit of a Vibhitaka tree, which Vahuka fells to check. In exchange for horse-lore, Rituparna teaches Vahuka the science of dice, and as Nala learns it Kali leaves his body and seeks shelter in the tree. Freed, Nala drives on toward Vidarbha, though he has not yet taken back his own form.

scenes.B03C072S01: A garment falls, Rituparna's counting feat is verified by felling the tree, the dice-for-horses bargain is struck, and Kali leaves Nala.

shots.B03C072S01H01: After a garment falls and a tree is counted and felled to prove Rituparna's skill, the two trade knowledge, and Kali leaves Nala and hides in the Vibhitaka tree.

B03C073.summary: Rituparna arrives at Kundina, the Vidarbha capital, and the rattle of his car stirs Damayanti, who half believes it is Nala's. Bhima welcomes the visitor, but Rituparna shows no sign of a swayamvara and says he came only to pay respects, which Bhima doubts. Damayanti, still unsure who the charioteer is, sends a messenger to find out.

scenes.B03C073S01: Rituparna reaches Bhima's court, Damayanti hears a car she takes for Nala's, and she sends a messenger to learn who the charioteer is.

shots.B03C073S01H01: The people announce Rituparna's arrival, his car is heard across the city, and Damayanti, believing it may be Nala's, laments and longs for him.
shots.B03C073S01H02: Rituparna greets Bhima, who finds no swayamvara preparations, and Rituparna says he came only to pay his respects, which Bhima suspects is not the real reason.
shots.B03C073S01H03: Vahuka stables the horses while Damayanti, unsure who the charioteer is, decides to send a female messenger to find out.

B03C074.summary: Damayanti sends Kesini to question the charioteer Vahuka, who offers a cover story about coming for a second swayamvara and says no one knows where Nala is. When Kesini repeats the words Parnada carried, Nala, still in disguise, is overcome and answers with a speech about the faithfulness of wives, then weeps. Kesini carries his reaction back to Damayanti.

scenes.B03C074S01: Kesini questions Vahuka, who gives a cover story, and then, on hearing the message, answers with a speech about faithful wives and weeps.

shots.B03C074S01H01: Damayanti tells Kesini to test the charioteer, and Vahuka gives an account of his master's journey and of Varshneya's departure while claiming no one knows Nala's whereabouts.
shots.B03C074S01H02: Hearing Kesini repeat the old words, Nala answers with a speech about patient, faithful wives, cannot hold back his tears, and Kesini goes back to report.
shots.B03C074S01H03: Heading: the next section, LXXV, begins here.

B03C075.summary: Damayanti, now suspecting that Vahuka is Nala, has Kesini watch him closely, and Kesini reports wonders such as widened passages, vessels filling with water, and fire lit from grass. Damayanti then tests him by tasting his cooking, recognizes Nala's hand in it, and sends her children to him. Nala embraces them in tears but sends Kesini away.

scenes.B03C075S01: Kesini reports Vahuka's marvels to Damayanti, who then tastes his cooking and recognizes Nala.

shots.B03C075S01H01: Damayanti asks Kesini to watch Vahuka closely, and Kesini reports a string of wonders, from widened passages and filling vessels to fire from sun-held grass and flowers made fragrant by pressing.
shots.B03C075S01H02: Damayanti has Kesini bring meat he cooked, recognizes Nala's cooking, and sends her children to him; Nala embraces them in tears and asks Kesini to leave, so that people will not talk.

B03C076.summary: Damayanti tells her mother she will examine Vahuka herself, and with her parents' consent Nala is brought to her apartments. She questions him about his desertion, and Nala blames Kali, the demon Damayanti had cursed, who had lodged in his body and has now left him. The Wind-god vouches for Damayanti, Nala resumes his own form, and the couple are reunited in Bhima's palace some four years after the loss of his kingdom.

scenes.B03C076S01: Damayanti questions Nala, who blames Kali, the Wind-god vouches for her, Nala regains his form, and the couple are reunited.

shots.B03C076S01H01: Damayanti questions Vahuka about his desertion, Nala blames Kali, the Wind-god vouches for Damayanti, Nala resumes his true form, and the couple spend happy days together in Bhima's palace.

B03C077.summary: The next morning Nala, with Damayanti at his side, pays his respects to Bhima, and the city celebrates his return. Rituparna asks Nala's forgiveness, and Nala gives back the horse-lore he had learned. Rituparna then leaves for his own city with another charioteer, and Nala soon departs from Kundina.

scenes.B03C077S01: Nala and Damayanti greet Bhima, the city rejoices, Rituparna and Nala exchange forgiveness and return the horse-lore, and Rituparna leaves.

shots.B03C077S01H01: Nala and Damayanti pay respects to Bhima, Rituparna asks forgiveness and gets back the horse-lore, and the story closes with Rituparna leaving and Nala soon departing Kundina.

B03C078.summary: Nala marches back into his own country with a modest army and challenges his brother Pushkara to a new game of dice, with Damayanti and everything else as the stake. Pushkara boasts and mocks him, but Nala wins back his kingdom and his brother's life in a single throw. He then spares Pushkara, blaming the earlier loss on Kali, and rules his restored kingdom to the people's delight.

scenes.B03C078S01: Nala challenges Pushkara to a rematch, wins back everything in one throw, and spares his brother.

shots.B03C078S01H01: Nala marches into his country and offers Pushkara a rematch of dice or battle with Damayanti and the kingdom at stake; Pushkara mocks him, the game is played, and Nala wins everything back and pardons his brother, blaming Kali for the earlier defeat.
shots.B03C078S01H02: Nala embraces Pushkara and sends him home after a month of hospitality, and Nala rules his kingdom to the delight of his subjects.

B03C079.summary: With the kingdom restored, Damayanti and her children are brought back and Nala rules happily, giving many sacrifices. Vrihadaswa tells Yudhishthira that Nala's story is a comfort in misfortune and offers to teach him the science of dice, so that he will not be caught out by a skilled gambler. Yudhishthira accepts the lore, and Vrihadaswa goes off to bathe.

scenes.B03C079S01: The restored Nala's happy reign is recounted, Vrihadaswa gives Yudhishthira the dice-lore, and news of Arjuna's penance begins to trouble Yudhishthira.

shots.B03C079S01H01: Damayanti returns with her children to a restored Nala, and Vrihadaswa presents the story as a comfort against misfortune and offers Yudhishthira the science of dice.
shots.B03C079S01H02: Yudhishthira asks for the dice-lore and receives it, and the sage goes off to bathe in the sacred waters of Hayasirsha.
shots.B03C079S01H03: Yudhishthira hears from visiting Brahmanas that Arjuna is performing harsh penance alone in the forest, and he grieves for his brother while seeking comfort from the Brahmanas there.

B03C080.summary: After Arjuna leaves Kamyaka, the Pandavas live in low spirits, still hunting game to offer to the Brahmanas. Janamejaya asks how his ancestors managed without the hero, and Vaisampayana describes how Draupadi, Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva each lament his absence. Sahadeva suggests leaving the forest, since nothing there feels pleasant without Arjuna.

scenes.B03C080S01: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas fared without Arjuna, and Vaisampayana tells how each brother and Draupadi laments his absence in Kamyaka.

shots.B03C080S01H01: Heading: the Tirtha-yatra Parva begins here.
shots.B03C080S01H02: Janamejaya asks how his grandsires passed their time in the forest without Arjuna, whose skill made him their protector.
shots.B03C080S01H03: Vaisampayana says the brothers were cheerless without Arjuna, and Draupadi and Bhima each speak of the emptiness the forest now has without him.
shots.B03C080S01H04: Nakula laments that Arjuna's feats are famous even among the gods, recalls the horses he brought from the north, and says he no longer wants to stay in Kamyaka.
shots.B03C080S01H05: Sahadeva recalls Arjuna's deeds, from his victories and his winning of wives at the Rajasuya to defeating Drupada to pay Drona's fee, and prefers to leave the forest.

B03C081.summary: Yudhishthira, saddened by his brothers' and Krishna's grief over Arjuna, greets the sage Narada and asks what merit comes from going round the earth to visit its sacred waters and shrines. Narada replies by recounting what Bhishma once heard from the sage Pulastya. The episode sets up the story of Bhishma's meeting with Pulastya.

scenes.B03C081S01: Narada appears to Yudhishthira, who asks about the merit of pilgrimage, and Narada begins a story of Bhishma meeting Pulastya.

shots.B03C081S01H01: Yudhishthira, troubled by his brothers' and Krishna's sorrow, honours the arriving Narada and asks what merit comes from visiting the sacred waters and shrines on earth.
shots.B03C081S01H02: Narada begins the tale of Bhishma, who during his Pitrya vow by the source of the Ganga met the sage Pulastya, worshipped him, and was filled with joy at his sight.

B03C082.summary: The sage Pulastya, pleased with Bhishma's humility and truthfulness, offers to grant him a wish, and Bhishma asks about the merit of visiting sacred bathing places, the tirthas. Pulastya explains that pilgrimage is open even to the poor and is greater than many costly sacrifices, and he singles out the Pushkara tirtha as the foremost. He then leads Bhishma through a long itinerary of holy sites, naming the merit that each one brings.

scenes.B03C082S01: Pulastya offers a boon, Bhishma asks about the merit of tirthas, Pulastya praises Pushkara and then lists a long route of other sacred sites with their rewards.

shots.B03C082S01H01: Pulastya is pleased with Bhishma's virtue and offers to grant him whatever he asks.
shots.B03C082S01H02: Bhishma says he is already content to have seen the sage, and asks him to explain the merit of going round the earth visiting tirthas.
shots.B03C082S01H03: Pulastya explains that the merit of tirthas comes from self-control and virtue, that they can be reached by people who lack wealth, and that Pushkara is among the holiest of them.
shots.B03C082S01H04: Pulastya praises Pushkara at length, saying that bathing there, feeding Brahmanas, and living there for a time bring the merit of great sacrifices.
shots.B03C082S01H05: Pulastya names a long route of further tirthas, each with the reward it brings, from Jamvu-marga and Kanwa's asylum to Prabhasa, Dwaravati and beyond.

B03C083.summary: Pulastya continues his guide to sacred bathing places, starting with Kurukshetra and naming dozens of tirthas, each with the reward it brings in cattle gifts, sacrifices or heavenly regions. The list includes the five lakes that Rama made from the blood of the Kshatriyas he slew, which the Pitris declared holy, and the sacred confluences and springs along the way. The discourse ends by calling Kurukshetra the northern sacrificial altar of the Grandsire.

scenes.B03C083S01: Pulastya's long itinerary runs through Kurukshetra and its many tirthas, including Rama's lakes, and closes by praising Kurukshetra.

shots.B03C083S01H01: Pulastya continues the itinerary from Kurukshetra, listing dozens of tirthas and their rewards, including Rama's lakes, and ends by praising Kurukshetra as the sacrificial altar of the Grandsire.

B03C084.summary: Pulastya carries on his list of holy bathing places, moving from the tirtha of Dharma and the Saraswati to the Himalayan source of the Ganges and onward to Naimisha, Gaya, and many other sites. Each place is tied to a reward, such as the merit of a horse-sacrifice, the gift of a thousand cows, or passage to a heavenly realm. The catalogue shows pilgrimage as a long, repeated circuit that a devoted person can complete.

scenes.B03C084S01: Pulastya continues the pilgrimage list through many tirthas across the land, each with its promised merit.

shots.B03C084S01H01: Pulastya's list runs on through many more tirthas, from Dharma's bathing place and the Ganges source to Naimisha, Gaya and the Gandaki, each promising a specific merit and ending with Lalitika.

B03C085.summary: Pulastya keeps listing sacred places, ranging from Samvedya and the Kaveri to Gokarna, Dandaka, and Kalanjara, and gives special praise to Prayaga, where the Ganga meets the Yamuna. He says that in the present age the Ganga alone is holy, and that reciting or hearing this account of the tirthas brings sons, wealth, and freedom from sin. Narada then tells Yudhishthira that Bhishma ended his own tour at Prayaga and encourages him to visit these places with the sages, and Yudhishthira begins to recite the merits to the ascetics.

scenes.B03C085S01: Pulastya's list of tirthas runs on, with Prayaga singled out, Pulastya explains the benefits of reciting it, and Narada encourages Yudhishthira to visit the places.

shots.B03C085S01H01: Pulastya lists more sacred places, from Samvedya and Lauhitya to the Kaveri, the Godavari and Dandaka, with the merit each one gives.
shots.B03C085S01H02: The list runs through Gokarna, Gayatri, Tungaka and Kalanjara, then praises Prayaga as the foremost tirtha of all, where the Ganga meets the Yamuna, and gives the age-by-age holiness of the Ganga and the other tirthas.
shots.B03C085S01H03: Pulastya advises that the account be recited only to worthy people, and promises that reciting or hearing it cleanses sins and brings boons such as sons, wealth and royal power.
shots.B03C085S01H04: Narada reports that Pulastya took his leave and that Bhishma ended his tour at Prayaga, then promises Yudhishthira fame and merit if he visits the tirthas with the sages, guided by Lomasa.
shots.B03C085S01H05: Vaisampayana says Narada departed, and Yudhishthira, reflecting on the matter, begins to recite the merits of the tirthas to the ascetics.

B03C086.summary: Having heard his brothers and Narada, Yudhishthira tells the sage Dhaumya that he sent Arjuna to win celestial weapons from Indra. He judges the Kaurava champions, especially Karna, to be a grave threat, and says only Arjuna can match them. He asks Dhaumya to name a new forest for the group, since they cannot bear to stay in Kamyaka without Arjuna.

scenes.B03C086S01: Yudhishthira explains to Dhaumya why he sent Arjuna to Indra, assesses the Kaurava warriors, and asks for a new forest to live in.

shots.B03C086S01H01: Yudhishthira tells Dhaumya that he sent Arjuna to gain weapons from Indra, names the Kaurava champions including Karna, judges Arjuna alone able to face them, and asks for a new forest to live in.

B03C087.summary: To comfort the grieving Pandavas, the priest Dhaumya begins a survey of holy places, starting with the eastern quarter. He names Naimisha, Gaya, the Ganga, Prayaga, Mahendra and Kundoda, tying many of them to famous sages and kings, including Nala's rest at Kundoda. He promises that visiting these sites brings far greater merit than hearing about them.

scenes.B03C087S01: Dhaumya surveys the holy places of the east, from Naimisha and Gaya to Prayaga, Mahendra and Kundoda.

shots.B03C087S01H01: Dhaumya comforts the Pandavas and introduces the eastern holy places he will describe, from Naimisha and Gaya through Prayaga and Mahendra to sites linked with sages and kings.

B03C088.summary: Dhaumya turns to the south, naming the Godavari, the Payoshni (where a tale of King Nriga is told), Gokarna, and Agastya's hermitage, and calling the Payoshni's water very cleansing. He then moves to Surashtra, describing Prabhasa, Pindaraka and Mount Ujjayanta. He ends with Dwaravati, where Krishna dwells, as a place of great merit.

scenes.B03C088S01: Dhaumya surveys the southern and Surashtra holy places, ending with Dwaravati, Krishna's city.

shots.B03C088S01H01: Dhaumya describes the southern holy places, from the Godavari and the Payoshni, where King Nriga's tale is set, to Gokarna, Devasabha and Agastya's hermitage.
shots.B03C088S01H02: Dhaumya moves to Surashtra, naming Prabhasa, Pindaraka and Mount Ujjayanta, and closes with Dwaravati, where Hari dwells, praising Krishna as the embodiment of virtue.

B03C089.summary: Dhaumya describes the western holy places, centered on the Narmada river, the Vaidurya peak and the Viswamitra river. He recalls how Yayati's fall from heaven happened on the banks of the Viswamitra river and names the Pushkara lake. He closes with a verse stating that even imagining a pilgrimage to Pushkara cleanses sin.

scenes.B03C089S01: Dhaumya surveys the western holy places, centered on the Narmada and the Pushkara lake, and closes with a verse about Pushkara.

shots.B03C089S01H01: Dhaumya lists the western sites, from the Narmada and the Vaidurya peak to Yayati's fall at the Viswamitra river and the Pushkara lake, and ends with a verse on how imagined pilgrimage to Pushkara cleanses sin.

B03C090.summary: Dhaumya finishes with the northern holy places, beginning with the Saraswati and Yamuna, where Sahadeva's sacrifice is recalled, and running on to Gangadwara and Badari. He describes Badari as the place where Narayana is worshipped by gods and sages, and he urges Yudhishthira to make the journey with the Brahmanas to ease his anxiety. The chapter then gives way to the next section.

scenes.B03C090S01: Dhaumya covers the northern holy places, from the Saraswati to Badari, and urges Yudhishthira to visit them.

shots.B03C090S01H01: Dhaumya describes the northern sites, from the Saraswati, the Yamuna and Sahadeva's sacrifice to Gangadwara and Badari, and urges Yudhishthira to visit them to be freed from anxiety.

B03C091.summary: The sage Lomasa arrives while Dhaumya is speaking and tells Yudhishthira that he saw Arjuna sitting beside Indra in heaven. Arjuna has won divine weapons from Rudra and other gods and has learned music and dance, and Indra promises that he will return soon. Indra also says Karna, though formidable, is far below Arjuna, and advises the brothers to practise asceticism while they wait.

scenes.B03C091S01: Lomasa arrives with news of Arjuna's gains in heaven, relays Indra's assurance about Karna, and passes on Indra's advice to the Pandavas.

shots.B03C091S01H01: Lomasa tells Yudhishthira that he has seen Arjuna in Indra's heaven, lists the weapons and arts Arjuna has gained, and relays Indra's word that Arjuna will return soon, that Karna is no match for him, and that the brothers should practise asceticism meanwhile.

B03C092.summary: Lomasa passes on Arjuna's request that he guard Yudhishthira through a tour of the tirthas, and Yudhishthira agrees at once. Lomasa advises him to travel light, and Yudhishthira sends away those who cannot bear hunger, cold, and the road. The citizens and Brahmanas return to Hastinapura, where Dhritarashtra provides for them, while Yudhishthira stays three nights at Kamyaka with a small company.

scenes.B03C092S01: Yudhishthira agrees to the pilgrimage, Lomasa advises a light retinue, and the larger company is sent back to Hastinapura.

shots.B03C092S01H01: Lomasa relays Arjuna's request that he guide Yudhishthira through the tirthas and guard them from Rakshasas, and says he will go along, as earlier royal sages did.
shots.B03C092S01H02: Yudhishthira is overjoyed, says he had already decided on the pilgrimage, and agrees to set out whenever Lomasa chooses.
shots.B03C092S01H03: Lomasa advises Yudhishthira to travel with a light retinue so that the journey will be easier.
shots.B03C092S01H04: Yudhishthira asks those who cannot bear the hardships of travel, and the cooks and dependants, to turn back, and sends the loyal citizens to Dhritarashtra for their allowances.
shots.B03C092S01H05: The citizens and Brahmanas return to Hastinapura, where Dhritarashtra provides for them, while Yudhishthira stays three nights at Kamyaka with a few Brahmanas and Lomasa.

B03C093.summary: The Brahmanas who have been living with the Pandavas in the forest ask to join the pilgrimage, since the tirthas are dangerous and infested by beasts and Rakshasas. Yudhishthira agrees, and Vyasa, Parvata and Narada advise him to purify both body and heart before setting out. The party then departs on an auspicious day, dressed in bark and hides and armed, facing east.

scenes.B03C093S01: The Brahmanas ask to join, Yudhishthira agrees, the sages give their advice, and the party sets out eastward.

shots.B03C093S01H01: The Brahmanas beg to join Yudhishthira on the pilgrimage, pointing out that the tirthas are dangerous and need protection from Rakshasas.
shots.B03C093S01H02: Yudhishthira agrees with tears of joy, and Vyasa, Parvata and Narada advise purifying the body by rule and the heart by goodwill toward all before visiting the tirthas.
shots.B03C093S01H03: After worship and rites, the party sets out in bark and hides, armed, with cooks and servants, facing east.

B03C094.summary: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa why his wicked enemies prosper while he suffers. Lomasa answers that sinners may prosper for a time but are finally ruined, citing the Asuras who fell through pride while the gods gained prosperity by virtue and visits to the tirthas. He urges Yudhishthira to follow the gods' example, citing kings who won fame that way, and predicts the sons of Dhritarashtra will be destroyed.

scenes.B03C094S01: Yudhishthira asks why his enemies prosper, and Lomasa explains that the gods prospered through virtue and tirtha visits, while the Asuras fell through pride.

shots.B03C094S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa why his sinful enemies prosper while he suffers.
shots.B03C094S01H02: Lomasa replies that sinners may prosper briefly but are finally ruined, recounting how the Asuras fell through pride, urging Yudhishthira to bathe at the tirthas like the gods, and predicting the destruction of Dhritarashtra's sons.

B03C095.summary: The Pandavas bathe and give gifts at several rivers, then keep a vow near the Brahmasara lake at Gayasira, joined by many Brahmanas. There Shamatha tells how King Gaya once held sacrifices with mountains of food and rivers of butter and curds, so lavish that the gifts could not be counted. The account shows the pilgrimage as a path of both penance and generosity.

scenes.B03C095S01: The Pandavas bathe at many sites, keep the Chaturmasya vow at Gayasira, and hear Shamatha recount King Gaya's vast sacrifices.

shots.B03C095S01H01: The Pandavas bathe and give gifts at the Gomati, Vahuda and Prayaga, then reach Gayasira and the Brahmasara lake, where they keep the Chaturmasya vow among many Brahmanas, and Shamatha recounts King Gaya's vast sacrifices.
shots.B03C095S01H02: Shamatha closes by noting that King Gaya held many such sacrifices beside this same Brahmasara.

B03C096.summary: At Agastya's hermitage Yudhishthira asks why Agastya killed the demon Vatapi, and Lomasa explains. The demon Ilwala, angered at being refused a son like Indra, turned his brother Vatapi into a ram, fed him to Brahmanas, and then tore them open when Vatapi answered his call. Agastya, finding his ancestors hanging head-down in a pit and wanting a son to free them, creates a woman, Lopamudra, who is raised as a princess of Vidarbha.

scenes.B03C096S01: Lomasa tells how Ilwala and Vatapi preyed on Brahmanas, then how Agastya, to save his ancestors, created Lopamudra, who was raised in Vidarbha.

shots.B03C096S01H01: Yudhishthira settles at Agastya's hermitage and asks why Agastya slew Vatapi and how strong that demon was.
shots.B03C096S01H02: Lomasa tells how the demon Ilwala, angered at being denied a son like Indra, turned his brother Vatapi into a ram, served him to Brahmanas, and called him back to tear them open.
shots.B03C096S01H03: Agastya finds his ancestors hanging head-down in a pit, who ask for offspring; he creates the woman Lopamudra, who is born to the king of Vidarbha and grows into a beautiful princess whom her father must find a husband for.

B03C097.summary: Agastya asks the king of Vidarbha for Lopamudra, and the king, though reluctant, gives her when she urges him to. Lopamudra gives up her fine robes for ascetic clothing, and the couple take up penance at Gangadwara. Later, when she asks for a bed and ornaments of a princess before intimacy, Agastya says he lacks the wealth and sets out to find it.

scenes.B03C097S01: Agastya marries Lopamudra, who asks for luxuries before intimacy, and he sets out to find wealth.

shots.B03C097S01H01: Agastya asks for Lopamudra's hand, the king and queen are distressed, Lopamudra urges her father to give her, and the couple take up penance at Gangadwara after she gives up her fine robes.
shots.B03C097S01H02: When Lopamudra, in her season, asks for a palace-style bed and ornaments, Agastya says he lacks such wealth, and she suggests he summon it by his power, which he refuses because it would cost his merit.
shots.B03C097S01H03: Agastya says he will go out to find wealth, and tells Lopamudra to stay and do as she pleases in the meantime.

B03C098.summary: Agastya goes to three wealthy kings in turn, Srutarvan, Vradhnaswa and Trasadasyu, asking for wealth without harming anyone. Each king says his spending matches his income, so Agastya, who will not take from anyone at another's cost, leaves empty-handed. The kings then propose asking the Danava Ilwala, the richest man on earth, and they all go to him.

scenes.B03C098S01: Agastya goes to three kings for wealth, each one says his spending equals his income, and they agree to go to Ilwala.

shots.B03C098S01H01: Agastya goes to King Srutarvan, who is wealthy, and asks for a share of his riches without harming others.
shots.B03C098S01H02: Srutarvan says his spending matches his income, and Agastya refuses to take anything, then goes with Srutarvan to King Vradhnaswa.
shots.B03C098S01H03: Vradhnaswa likewise says his spending equals his income, so Agastya and the two kings go on to Trasadasyu, the wealthy son of Purokutsa.
shots.B03C098S01H04: Trasadasyu says the same, and the kings suggest asking the Danava Ilwala, the richest man on earth, for wealth.
shots.B03C098S01H05: The company agrees that begging from Ilwala is the right course, and they all go to him together.

B03C099.summary: Ilwala welcomes Agastya and the kings and serves them his brother Vatapi as cooked meat, but Agastya digests the demon, and Ilwala, learning this, gives the party a golden car and wealth. Lopamudra asks for one powerful son, who is born after seven years as Dridhasyu, later called Idhmavaha. Lomasa then tells the story of Rama of Bhrigu's line, who lost his energy to Rama, son of Dasaratha, and regained it at a sacred river.

scenes.B03C099S01: Agastya digests Vatapi, Ilwala gives wealth and a golden car, Agastya's son Dridhasyu is born, and Lomasa begins the story of Rama of Bhrigu's line.
scenes.B03C099S02: Rama of Bhrigu's line is humbled by Rama, son of Dasaratha, and regains his energy at a sacred river on the Pitris' advice.

shots.B03C099S01H01: Ilwala serves Vatapi to Agastya and the kings, Agastya digests him when Ilwala calls, and Agastya then asks for wealth and offers Lopamudra a choice of sons, to which she answers that one powerful son is best.
shots.B03C099S01H02: Lopamudra conceives, Agastya retreats to the forest, and after seven years the son Dridhasyu is born, earning the name Idhmavaha for carrying sacred wood.
shots.B03C099S01H03: Lomasa explains how the asylum got its name, praises the Bhagirathi and Bhrigu's tirtha, and says that bathing there restored Rama's might, which Yudhishthira may likewise recover from Duryodhana.
shots.B03C099S01H04: Yudhishthira bathes with his brothers and Krishna, his body blazes with new brilliance, and he asks why Rama's energy was once taken and how he got it back.
shots.B03C099S01H05: Lomasa begins the story: Vishnu was born as Rama, son of Dasaratha, and Rama of Bhrigu's line came to Ayodhya to test him by having him string his bow.
shots.B03C099S02H01: Dasaratha's son strings the bow, reveals a vision of the cosmos, and Bhrigu's Rama is stripped of his energy until the Pitris send him to a sacred river, where he recovers it.

B03C100.summary: Lomasa now recounts Agastya's deeds, beginning with the Kalakeya Danavas, who under Vritra harried the gods. Brahma advised the gods to ask the sage Dadhicha for his bones, and Dadhicha, giving up his life, let Twashtri forge them into the Vajra for Indra. The episode explains the origin of the weapon that will later be used against Vritra.

scenes.B03C100S01: Vritra and the Kalakeyas trouble the gods, and Dadhicha gives his bones to make the Vajra.

shots.B03C100S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa to describe Agastya's exploits in detail.
shots.B03C100S01H02: Lomasa tells how Vritra's Kalakeya Danavas harried the gods, how Brahma advised seeking Dadhicha's bones, and how Dadhicha gave his life and Twashtri forged the Vajra for Indra.

B03C101.summary: Armed with the Vajra and strengthened by Vishnu and the sages, Indra attacks Vritra, who is guarded by the Kalakeyas. Vritra is struck down, but Indra flees in doubt about whether the foe is really dead, and the leaderless Danavas retreat into the sea. There they plot to destroy the ascetics, on whom the worlds depend.

scenes.B03C101S01: Indra, empowered by the gods, slays Vritra with the Vajra, and the Danavas retreat into the sea and plot against the ascetics.

shots.B03C101S01H01: Indra, empowered by Vishnu, the gods and sages, attacks Vritra and slays him with the Vajra, then the Danavas retreat into the sea and plot the destruction of the ascetics.

B03C102.summary: The Kalakeyas hide in the sea by day and come out by night to devour sages in their hermitages, including those of Vasishtha, Chyavana and Bharadwaja. Men find the mutilated bodies each morning, and sacrifices and sacred studies come to a halt. The gods, unable to stop the killings, turn to Narayana for protection.

scenes.B03C102S01: The Kalakeyas kill ascetics in their hermitages at night, and the gods seek protection from Narayana.

shots.B03C102S01H01: Lomasa describes how the Kalakeyas, sheltering in the sea, killed sages in their hermitages at night, halting sacrifices, and how the gods appeal to Narayana for protection.

B03C103.summary: The gods tell Vishnu that the killing of Brahmanas threatens earth and heaven alike. Vishnu explains that the Kalakeyas are hiding in the ocean and can be reached only if the sea is dried up, which only Agastya can do. The gods then go to Agastya and praise him as the one who has always protected them.

scenes.B03C103S01: The gods plead with Vishnu, who names Agastya as the only one who can dry up the sea, and the gods approach Agastya in praise.

shots.B03C103S01H01: The gods tell Vishnu that the killing of Brahmanas threatens the whole universe and beg him to act.
shots.B03C103S01H02: Vishnu says only Agastya can dry up the sea where the Kalakeyas hide, so the gods go to Agastya and praise him as their protector.

B03C104.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Vindhya suddenly swelled with wrath, and Lomasa explains. Vindhya, jealous of Meru around which the sun circles, demanded that the sun circle him too, and then grew tall enough to block the sun and moon. The gods asked Agastya to intervene, and he promised to go south and asked Vindhya to wait for his return; since he never came back, Vindhya has stayed low. The gods then request that Agastya drink the ocean so that the Kalakeyas can be destroyed, and he agrees.

scenes.B03C104S01: Lomasa explains why Vindhya stopped growing, then tells how the gods asked Agastya to drink the ocean.

shots.B03C104S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why Vindhya suddenly grew huge in his anger.
shots.B03C104S01H02: Lomasa explains that Vindhya, jealous of Meru, demanded that the sun circle him as well, and then grew to obstruct the sun, so the gods went to Agastya.
shots.B03C104S01H03: The gods ask Agastya to stop Vindhya, and he asks the mountain to make way for his trip south until he returns, a promise that keeps Vindhya low because Agastya never came back.
shots.B03C104S01H04: The gods ask Agastya to drink the ocean so they can destroy the Kalakeyas, he agrees, and he sets out for the sea with sages, gods and other beings following.

B03C105.summary: Agastya drinks up the ocean while the gods praise him and slay the Kalakeyas, and some of the survivors flee into the netherworld. When the gods ask him to refill the sea, Agastya says the water has been digested and that they must find another way. The gods and the sages part in wonder and sorrow, and then gather with Vishnu and Brahma to consider how to refill it.

scenes.B03C105S01: Agastya drinks the ocean, the gods slay the Kalakeyas, and Agastya says the water cannot be restored.

shots.B03C105S01H01: Agastya drinks up the sea while the gods praise him and slay the Kalakeyas, and when asked to refill it he says the water is digested, so the gods must find another way.

B03C106.summary: Brahma tells the gods that refilling the ocean must wait for the descendants of Bhagiratha's family. Yudhishthira asks Lomasa to tell how that family refilled the sea, and Lomasa begins with King Sagara. Sagara, childless, prayed to Shiva on Mount Kailasa and was promised many sons, and when his queen bore a gourd, a voice from the sky told him to keep its seeds in vessels.

scenes.B03C106S01: Brahma delays the refilling of the ocean, and Lomasa introduces Sagara, whose prayer to Shiva brings a promise of many sons.

shots.B03C106S01H01: Brahma tells the gods they must wait, since the ocean will be refilled through the descendants of Bhagiratha's family.
shots.B03C106S01H02: Yudhishthira asks how Bhagiratha's kin refilled the ocean and asks Lomasa to tell of the achievements of King Sagara.
shots.B03C106S01H03: Vaisampayana says Lomasa begins to narrate the achievements of King Sagara.
shots.B03C106S01H04: Lomasa describes Sagara, who was childless and prayed to Shiva on Mount Kailasa, and was promised sixty thousand sons; his queens bore a gourd and a boy, and a voice from the sky told him to keep the gourd's seeds in vessels.

B03C107.summary: The seeds in the gourd grow into sixty thousand violent sons who terrorize people and even the gods, and Brahma foretells their doom. When the horse of Sagara's sacrifice vanishes at the sea, the sons dig up the ocean in search of it and are burned to ashes by the sage Kapila. Sagara sends his grandson Ansuman, who recovers the horse and wins Kapila's favor, and the story points ahead to Bhagiratha, who will bring the Ganga down to earth.

scenes.B03C107S01: The sixty thousand sons are born and destroyed by Kapila's fire, Sagara banishes Asamanjas, and Ansuman wins back the horse and Kapila's favor.

shots.B03C107S01H01: The sixty thousand sons grow fierce and harass gods and men, Brahma foretells their doom, and when Sagara's sacrificial horse vanishes at the sea, the sons search the world and, failing, are ordered by their angry father never to return without it.
shots.B03C107S01H02: The sons dig into the sea toward the netherworld, find the horse beside the sage Kapila, and are burned to ashes; Narada reports this to Sagara, who sends for his grandson Ansuman.
shots.B03C107S01H03: Yudhishthira asks why Sagara abandoned his own valiant son.
shots.B03C107S01H04: Lomasa explains that Asamanjas, Sagara's son by the princess of Sivi, threw townsmen's children into the river, the townspeople begged for relief, and Sagara banished him.
shots.B03C107S01H05: Sagara sends Ansuman to win back the horse, Kapila grants Ansuman's wish for the horse and for his ancestors' purification, the sacrifice is finished, and the line passes to Dilipa and then Bhagiratha, who will try to bring the Ganga down.

B03C108.summary: Bhagiratha, grandson of Ansuman, grieves over his ancestors' fate and goes to the Himalayas to perform austerities for a thousand years. When Ganga appears, he asks her to descend to earth and wash the ashes of the sons of Sagara so they can enter heaven. Ganga agrees, but warns that only Shiva can bear the force of her fall, so Bhagiratha wins Shiva's favor.

scenes.B03C108S01: Bhagiratha performs austerities, Ganga appears and agrees to descend, and Bhagiratha secures Shiva's favor to bear her fall.

shots.B03C108S01H01: Bhagiratha, grieving over his ancestors, hands over his kingdom and performs austerities for a thousand years in the Himalayas, which are described in lush detail.
shots.B03C108S01H02: Ganga appears and asks what he wants, and Bhagiratha asks her to wash the bodies of the sons of Sagara so they can reach heaven.
shots.B03C108S01H03: Ganga agrees but warns that only Shiva can bear her fall, so Bhagiratha goes to Kailasa and wins Shiva's favor to sustain her descent.

B03C109.summary: Shiva agrees to bear Ganga's descent, and when the river comes down from the sky she divides into three streams and follows Bhagiratha to the sea, which she fills. Bhagiratha adopts Ganga as a daughter and offers water to his ancestors. Lomasa ends by summarizing how the sea was drunk, how Ganga was brought down, and how Vatapi was destroyed.

scenes.B03C109S01: Shiva agrees to hold Ganga's fall, Ganga descends and follows Bhagiratha to the sea, and Lomasa closes his account.

shots.B03C109S01H01: Shiva agrees to bear Ganga's fall, Ganga comes down in three streams and follows Bhagiratha to fill the sea, and Lomasa ends by recalling how the sea was drunk, Ganga brought down, and Vatapi slain.

B03C110.summary: Yudhishthira and his brothers reach the Hemakuta hill, where strange things happen, and Lomasa explains that a wrathful sage named Rishava made the hill forbid speech. He tells how the gods hid the place from mortals and then sends the party on to the Kausiki river and Kasyapa's hermitage. He then tells the story of Rishyasringa, the horned sage born to a hind, and how Indra was made to send rain to the land of Lomapada.

scenes.B03C110S01: The Pandavas see strange sights at Hemakuta, Lomasa explains their cause and points out nearby hermitages, and he tells how Rishyasringa was born and why Indra's rain stopped.

shots.B03C110S01H01: Yudhishthira and his brothers see strange sights on the Hemakuta hill, where speech brings stones and storms, and Yudhishthira asks Lomasa about them.
shots.B03C110S01H02: Lomasa explains that a wrathful sage named Rishava made the hill forbid speech, that the gods hid the place from mortals, and that bathing there cleanses sin, and he sends the party on to the Kausiki.
shots.B03C110S01H03: Lomasa names the hermitages of Viswamitra and of Kasyapa, whose son Rishyasringa made Indra send rain and was given the princess Santa by King Lomapada.
shots.B03C110S01H04: Yudhishthira asks how Rishyasringa was born of a hind, why Indra feared him, and what Santa was like, and he asks Lomasa to tell the whole story.
shots.B03C110S01H05: Lomasa tells how Vibhandaka's seed fell into a hind to produce Rishyasringa, the horn-headed sage raised without any woman, and how Lomapada, facing drought and the Brahmanas' anger, decided to bring the sage to his land.

B03C111.summary: Lomapada's courtesans prepare a floating hermitage near the hut of the young sage Rishyasringa, and send a clever courtesan to win his trust. She plies him with gifts, embraces and games until he is overcome with love and sits sighing. When his father Vibhandaka finds him in this state, he asks who has been to the hermitage.

scenes.B03C111S01: The courtesan approaches Rishyasringa at his hermitage, talks with him, and offers him fruit, and he offers ripe fruit in return.
scenes.B03C111S02: The courtesan tempts Rishyasringa with gifts and embraces until he is overcome with love, and his father Vibhandaka finds him distressed.

shots.B03C111S01H01: The courtesan prepares a floating hermitage near Kasyapa's son's hut and sends her daughter, a clever courtesan, who finds Rishyasringa.
shots.B03C111S01H02: The courtesan greets Rishyasringa with courteous questions about his austerities, his father and his studies.
shots.B03C111S01H03: Rishyasringa welcomes her, offers water, fruit and a seat, and asks what vow she is keeping.
shots.B03C111S01H04: She explains that her hermitage lies three yojanas away and that her vow requires him to embrace her.
shots.B03C111S01H05: Rishyasringa offers her ripe fruits instead, such as gallnuts and myrobalans.
shots.B03C111S02H01: She discards the fruit, gives him garlands, drink and playful embraces, then leaves pretending to make offerings, and Rishyasringa, overcome with love, sighs until his father Vibhandaka finds him and asks who has come.

B03C112.summary: Rishyasringa tells his father Vibhandaka about the visitor who came to his hermitage, describing her beauty, her ornaments, and the fruit and drink she offered him. He says her departure has left him longing for her and eager to follow her and take up the same austerities. The account shows how deeply the courtesan's visit has disturbed his mind.

scenes.B03C112S01: Rishyasringa describes the visitor to his father, her gifts and her departure, and says he longs to follow her.

shots.B03C112S01H01: Rishyasringa describes the visitor's beauty, dress and gifts to his father, and says he is pining and wants to follow her and live the same austere life.

B03C114.summary: Yudhishthira bathes where the Ganga meets the sea and travels toward the land of the Kalinga tribes. Lomasa tells how Rudra seized a sacrificial beast and was appeased by the gods, and how the Earth, given away to Kasyapa, rose up as an altar into the sea so that mortals could cross it. He instructs Yudhishthira to recite a formula and mount the altar, and Yudhishthira does so, then spends the night on Mount Mahendra.

scenes.B03C114S01: Yudhishthira bathes at the Ganga's mouth, Lomasa tells of Rudra and of the Earth's altar, and Yudhishthira is given the formula for crossing the sea.
scenes.B03C114S02: Yudhishthira completes the rites, enters the sea, and spends the night at the skirts of Mount Mahendra.

shots.B03C114S01H01: Yudhishthira bathes where the Ganga meets the sea and walks along the shore toward Kalinga country.
shots.B03C114S01H02: Lomasa describes the Vaitarani river, where Rudra seized a sacrificial beast and was appeased by the gods, who then reserved a best share for him.
shots.B03C114S01H03: Yudhishthira, his brothers and Draupadi bathe in the Vaitarani and make offerings to their ancestors.
shots.B03C114S01H04: Yudhishthira marvels at the power of pious acts and hears the sound of forest dwellers reciting prayers.
shots.B03C114S01H05: Lomasa explains the far-off sound, recounts how the Earth, given to Kasyapa, rose as an altar into the sea after he appeased her, and tells Yudhishthira to recite a formula and mount it to cross the sea.
shots.B03C114S02H01: Yudhishthira completes the rites, goes into the sea, and spends the night at the skirts of Mount Mahendra.

B03C115.summary: Yudhishthira spends a night among the sages, and Akritavrana, a follower of Parasurama, says Rama will appear on the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight. Asked about Rama's wars against the warrior class, Akritavrana begins with the thousand-armed Arjuna of the Haihayas, whom Vishnu was asked to kill, and then tells how the sage Richika won Satyavati from King Gadhi with a thousand horses from Varuna. Bhrigu's blessing for the couple sets up the birth of Jamadagni and, later, of Rama.

scenes.B03C115S01: Akritavrana predicts Rama's visit and tells of Arjuna of the Haihayas and of Richika's marriage to Satyavati.
scenes.B03C115S02: Bhrigu's boon for his daughter-in-law and her mother gives rise to the birth of Jamadagni.

shots.B03C115S01H01: Yudhishthira spends the night among the sages, honouring them, and asks Akritavrana when Parasurama, the descendant of Bhrigu, will appear.
shots.B03C115S01H02: Akritavrana says Rama, who knows of the visit, will appear to the sages on the fourteenth day of the fortnight, dressed in black deerskin with matted hair.
shots.B03C115S01H03: Yudhishthira asks Akritavrana to tell how Rama defeated the warriors and what caused their conflicts.
shots.B03C115S01H04: Akritavrana begins with Arjuna of the Haihayas, the thousand-armed king who oppressed the world until Vishnu was asked to kill him, and introduces Richika's marriage to Gadhi's daughter and Gadhi's demand for a dowry of horses.
shots.B03C115S01H05: Richika obtains a thousand horses from Varuna, marries Satyavati, and Bhrigu, pleased, grants a boon to the two women.
shots.B03C115S02H01: Bhrigu reveals that the pots and trees were swapped, asks that the warrior nature pass to Satyavati's grandson instead of her son, and Jamadagni is born, growing learned and gaining the arts of war.

B03C113.summary: Vibhandaka warns his son that the visitors were demons in lovely form, but while he is away searching for the courtesan, Rishyasringa is carried off on a floating hermitage to King Lomapada's land. The king gives Rishyasringa his daughter Santa, and rain returns to the land. To calm Vibhandaka's anger, the king arranges herds and ploughed fields along his route for his son, and the father is appeased and blesses the couple.

scenes.B03C113S01: Vibhandaka warns his son, the courtesans take him to the king, the king marries him to Santa, and the king pacifies Vibhandaka with herds and fields; Lomasa then points Yudhishthira to a holy lake.

shots.B03C113S01H01: Vibhandaka warns that the visitors were demons; Rishyasringa is lured onto the floating hermitage to the king, who gives him Santa and brings rain, and then arranges cattle and fields to appease the angry father.
shots.B03C113S01H02: The angry Vibhandaka, finding cowherds and fields that belong to his son, is appeased, sees Santa and his son, and blesses them, and Lomasa then sends Yudhishthira on to the holy lake.

B03C116.summary: Jamadagni marries Renuka, and their youngest son Rama is the most gifted of their five sons. When Renuka is stirred by desire at the sight of a king bathing, Jamadagni curses his elder sons for failing to act, and at his command Rama beheads his mother. Jamadagni grants Rama a boon that restores her, but later Arjuna's sons kill Jamadagni while Rama is away, and Rama returns to find his father dead.

scenes.B03C116S01: Renuka's lapse, Rama's obedience, the restoration of his mother by boon, Arjuna's raid on the hermitage, and Jamadagni's death.

shots.B03C116S01H01: Akritavrana recounts how Jamadagni married Renuka, how she was stirred by a king in the water and Rama beheaded her at his father's command, how Rama won a boon to restore her, and how Arjuna's sons killed Jamadagni while Rama was away, leaving Rama grieving.

B03C117.summary: Rama mourns his father, cremates him, and vows to wipe out the warrior caste, killing Kartavirya's sons and then exterminating the Kshatriyas seven times over. He makes five lakes of blood at Samantapanchaka, offers the earth to the priests, and gives an altar to Kasyapa before withdrawing to Mahendra. On the fourteenth day he appears to Yudhishthira and his brothers and honours the Brahmanas before the Pandavas head south.

scenes.B03C117S01: Rama laments and vows vengeance, wipes out the warriors, and retires to Mahendra; he then appears to Yudhishthira and his brothers and honours the Brahmanas.

shots.B03C117S01H01: Rama laments his father's death, cremates him, and vows to wipe out the warrior caste, killing Kartavirya's sons and seven times exterminating the Kshatriyas, forming five lakes of blood, then giving the earth to the priests and an altar to Kasyapa before withdrawing to Mahendra.
shots.B03C117S01H02: On the fourteenth day Rama appears to Yudhishthira and his brothers, who honour him and the Brahmanas, and after a night on Mahendra the Pandavas set out southward.

B03C118.summary: Yudhishthira travels along the coast, bathing at many tirthas, including the Godavari and Agastya's holy spot in the Dravida country. He gives away cows, visits the altar of Richika's son and many shrines of the gods, and fasts for twelve days at Prabhasa. There the Vrishnis, led by Valarama and Krishna, come to see him and weep at the wretched state of the Pandavas.

scenes.B03C118S01: Yudhishthira visits sacred places along the coast, fasts at Prabhasa, and is met by the Vrishnis, who weep at the Pandavas' condition.

shots.B03C118S01H01: Yudhishthira bathes at sacred places along the coast, visits shrines of many gods, fasts at Prabhasa, and is then met by the Vrishnis, led by Valarama and Krishna, who weep at the sight of the Pandavas' wretched state.

B03C119.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas and the Vrishnis discussed at Prabhasa. Valarama, seeing Yudhishthira in misery, denounces the Kuru elders and the prosperity of Duryodhana, and wonders whether virtue brings any reward. He lists the brothers' heroic qualities and asks why they must suffer so in the forest.

scenes.B03C119S01: Janamejaya asks about the meeting, and Valarama laments the Pandavas' suffering and attacks the Kuru elders and Duryodhana.

shots.B03C119S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what the Pandavas and the Vrishnis said and did together at Prabhasa.
shots.B03C119S01H02: Valarama, seeing Yudhishthira wretched, denounces the Kuru elders and Duryodhana's prosperity, lists each brother's heroic skills, and asks how they can bear their exile.

B03C120.summary: Satyaki urges an immediate attack on Duryodhana with the Vrishni army, naming their warriors and vowing victory. Krishna replies that Yudhishthira will accept sovereignty only if it is won by his own arms, and that the allies should stand together in any case. Yudhishthira sends the Vrishnis home, and he goes on with Lomasa to the Payosini river.

scenes.B03C120S01: Satyaki urges war, Krishna explains Yudhishthira's pride, and Yudhishthira sends the Vrishnis home and proceeds to the Payosini.

shots.B03C120S01H01: Satyaki urges Rama and Krishna not to lament but to march the Vrishni army at once against Dhritarashtra's sons, naming warriors such as Pradyumna, Samva and Abhimanyu, and vowing to slay Duryodhana.
shots.B03C120S01H02: Krishna agrees that the war is just, but says Yudhishthira will take sovereignty only by his own prowess, and that the Pandavas' allies should join their strength.
shots.B03C120S01H04: Yudhishthira says truth comes before power, asks the Vrishnis to go home, and promises to meet them again when the time for battle comes.
shots.B03C120S01H05: The Vrishnis and Pandavas part with greetings and embraces, and Yudhishthira goes on with Lomasa to the Payosini, where Brahmanas greet him.

B03C121.summary: Lomasa describes the lavish sacrifices that Nriga, Amurtarayasa and Gaya held on the Payosini, honouring Indra with Soma and paying priests immense gifts, and says a bath there brings Gaya's reward. Yudhishthira bathes there, then visits the sapphire hill and the Narmada, where Lomasa names the holy sites and Brahmanas receive gifts. Lomasa then speaks of Chyavana's feud with Indra, and Yudhishthira asks for the full story.

scenes.B03C121S01: Lomasa describes the sacrifices on the Payosini and the holy sites near the Narmada, and Yudhishthira asks about Chyavana and Indra.

shots.B03C121S01H01: Lomasa describes sacrifices held by Nriga, Amurtarayasa and Gaya on the Payosini, with rich gifts to the priests, and says that a bath there brings Gaya's reward.
shots.B03C121S01H02: Yudhishthira and his brothers bathe in the Payosini, then visit the sapphire hill and the Narmada, where Lomasa names the holy places and Brahmanas receive gifts.
shots.B03C121S01H03: Lomasa says that bathing on the sapphire hill and in the Narmada brings the regions of gods and kings, and recalls Saryati's sacrifice and Chyavana's feud with Indra.
shots.B03C121S01H04: Yudhishthira asks how Chyavana paralysed Indra and how the celestial physicians came to drink Soma.

B03C122.summary: Chyavana, son of Bhrigu, sits in meditation until an anthill covers him. King Saryati's daughter Sukanya, playing in the woods, pokes the glowing eyes in the anthill with thorns, blinding the sage, who then blocks the army's calls of nature. Saryati asks for forgiveness, and Chyavana agrees to pardon the king on condition that he gives Sukanya to him as his wife.

scenes.B03C122S01: Sukanya blinds Chyavana, the army is afflicted, and Saryati gives his daughter to the sage.

shots.B03C122S01H01: Chyavana, sitting motionless, is covered by an anthill; Sukanya pokes his eyes with thorns, the sage blocks the army's calls of nature, and Saryati, seeking the cause, asks forgiveness and is told he must give his daughter to the sage.
shots.B03C122S01H02: Saryati gives his daughter to Chyavana, who accepts her, and Sukanya attends her husband with devoted service.

B03C123.summary: The twin Ashvins see Sukanya bathing, mock her for marrying an aged man, and urge her to choose one of them instead. She refuses, and they offer to make Chyavana young again if she chooses one of them. After all three enter a pool and come out looking alike, Sukanya recognizes her own husband, and Chyavana promises that the Ashvins will drink Soma in Indra's presence.

scenes.B03C123S01: The Ashvins tempt Sukanya, restore Chyavana to youth, and Chyavana promises to make them Soma-drinkers.

shots.B03C123S01H01: The Ashvins see Sukanya bathing, ask whose daughter she is, and mock her for serving a decrepit old husband.
shots.B03C123S01H02: Sukanya refuses them, and the Ashvins offer to restore Chyavana to youth if she chooses one of them; she tells her husband, all three enter the water, and she recognizes her own husband among the identical young men.
shots.B03C123S01H03: Chyavana, now young and beautiful, promises the Ashvins that he will make them Soma-drinkers before the lord of gods, and they ascend to heaven while the couple live happily.

B03C124.summary: Saryati hears that Chyavana has become young and visits the hermitage, and Chyavana agrees to officiate at his sacrifice. When Chyavana prepares Soma for the Ashvins, Indra forbids it, arguing that they are only physicians. Chyavana defies him, paralyses Indra's arm when he raises the thunderbolt, and creates a monstrous demon named Mada to devour Indra.

scenes.B03C124S01: Chyavana officiates for Saryati, Indra opposes the offering to the Ashvins, and Chyavana summons the demon Mada.

shots.B03C124S01H01: Saryati visits and delights in the youthful couple, Chyavana agrees to officiate, and when he prepares Soma for the Ashvins, Indra protests that the twins are mere physicians with no right to it.
shots.B03C124S01H02: Chyavana defies Indra, paralyses his arm when Indra raises the thunderbolt, and conjures a huge demon named Mada to devour the god.

B03C125.summary: Frightened by the demon Mada, Indra agrees that the Ashvins shall have a right to Soma, and Chyavana disperses Mada among drink, women, dice and hunting. Chyavana then lives happily with Sukanya. Lomasa directs Yudhishthira to the lake, the Archika hill and other holy sites along the Yamuna, naming the sages and gods who worshipped there.

scenes.B03C125S01: Indra accepts the Ashvins' right to Soma, Chyavana scatters Mada, and Lomasa lists the holy places for Yudhishthira to visit.

shots.B03C125S01H01: Indra, terrified by Mada, agrees that the Ashvins may drink Soma; Chyavana scatters the demon among drink, women, dice and hunting; and Lomasa directs Yudhishthira to the lake, Archika hill and Yamuna sites where sages and gods worshipped.

B03C126.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Mandhata was born and how he became so powerful. Lomasa tells how the childless king Yuvanaswa drank by mistake a jar of water consecrated for another king's wife, and how a son came out of his side; Indra gave his finger to the infant to suck, which gave him the name Mandhata. The boy grew into a mighty ruler who conquered the three worlds, performed great sacrifices and ended a long drought.

scenes.B03C126S01: Yudhishthira asks about Mandhata, and Lomasa recounts his unusual birth, his rule, and the sacrifices and rain he brought, before Yudhishthira turns to Somaka.

shots.B03C126S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa how Mandhata, Yuvanaswa's son, was born and how he gained his power and name.
shots.B03C126S01H02: Lomasa tells how childless Yuvanaswa, athirst after a fast, drank the consecrated water from Bhrigu's hermitage, how a son came out of his side, how Indra's finger named him Mandhata, and how the boy grew to conquer the three worlds, perform sacrifices and end a drought.
shots.B03C126S01H03: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira then asks Lomasa about Somaka.

B03C127.summary: Somaka, a king with a hundred wives, finally has a single son, Jantu, and when an ant stings the boy, the commotion brings the king to the women's quarters. Somaka laments that one son is a burden and asks his priest for a rite that would give him a hundred sons. The priest says such a rite exists, but it requires a sacrifice of Jantu, which Somaka agrees to.

scenes.B03C127S01: Jantu is stung, Somaka laments his single son, and he asks the priest for a rite to get a hundred sons.
scenes.B03C127S02: The priest proposes that Jantu be the sacrificial victim, with the smoke of his fat to bring the sons.

shots.B03C127S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa about the power and deeds of King Somaka.
shots.B03C127S01H02: Lomasa tells how Somaka, with a hundred wives, has only one son, Jantu, and how an ant's sting makes the boy scream, bringing the king to the women's quarters.
shots.B03C127S01H03: Somaka laments that one son is a burden, that he is old, and asks whether any rite exists to get a hundred sons.
shots.B03C127S01H04: The family priest says that such a rite exists, if Somaka is able to perform it.
shots.B03C127S01H05: Somaka says he will do whatever the rite requires, and asks the priest to explain it.
shots.B03C127S02H01: The priest proposes that Jantu be the sacrificial victim, so that the mothers, breathing the smoke of his fat, will bear a hundred sons, and Jantu will be reborn with a golden mark.

B03C128.summary: The priest sacrifices Jantu despite the mothers' cries, and after the smoke reaches them, they all conceive and bear a hundred sons. Later Somaka finds his priest tormented in hell for officiating, and insists on sharing his fate, which Dharmaraja allows for the same period. After both work off their sins they are freed and enjoy their rewards together.

scenes.B03C128S01: The sacrifice of Jantu and the birth of a hundred sons, followed by the priest's punishment in hell and Somaka's choice to share it.
scenes.B03C128S02: Somaka and the priest work off their sins and are freed, and Lomasa recommends six nights of self-control at this hermitage.

shots.B03C128S01H01: Somaka agrees to whatever rite the priest orders, so that he may have many sons.
shots.B03C128S01H02: The mothers try to save Jantu, but the priest drags him away and sacrifices him; the mothers faint at the smoke, then all conceive, and a hundred sons are born, with Jantu the eldest.
shots.B03C128S01H03: After death Somaka sees the priest in hell and asks why; the priest explains that it is the result of officiating at the sacrifice, and Somaka asks Dharmaraja to free him.
shots.B03C128S01H04: Dharmaraja replies that no one can suffer for another's deeds, but Somaka insists on sharing the priest's fate, since their deeds are identical.
shots.B03C128S01H05: Dharmaraja agrees that Somaka may share the priest's fruit for the same time, after which both will go to the blessed regions.
shots.B03C128S02H01: Lomasa says the king and the priest worked off their sins, were freed, and shared their rewards, and he recommends six nights of self-control at this hermitage for those who seek heaven.

B03C129.summary: Lomasa names sacred sites along the Yamuna and in the Kuru field, recalling how Ishtikrita, Amvarisha, Yayati, Bharata and Marutta performed great rites and gave lavish gifts there. He says that bathing at these places lets one see all the worlds. Yudhishthira bathes and says that from there he can even see Arjuna.

scenes.B03C129S01: Lomasa names the sacred sites along the Yamuna and in the Kuru field, Yudhishthira bathes, and he says he can see Arjuna from there.

shots.B03C129S01H01: Lomasa names sacred sites on the Yamuna and in the Kuru field, where great rites and gifts were performed by Amvarisha, Yayati, Bharata and Marutta, and says that bathing there lets one behold all worlds.
shots.B03C129S01H02: Yudhishthira bathes with his brothers and says that through this rite he can see all the worlds, and even Arjuna, the rider of the white steed.
shots.B03C129S01H03: Lomasa confirms that the saints see all regions from here, and points to the holy Saraswati, the altar of the lord of beings and the field of the Kurus.

B03C130.summary: Lomasa points out a long series of sacred places, including the spot where the Saraswati vanishes underground, the Vipasa river where Vasistha was freed from his bonds, and the site where Lopamudra took Agastya as her lord. He notes that people who die at these sites are said to reach heaven, and that Shiva may be seen at the end of each age. He ends by telling how Usinara's sacrifice was tested by Indra and Agni in the form of a hawk and a pigeon.

scenes.B03C130S01: Lomasa names a series of sacred sites, from the Saraswati to Lopamudra's place, and ends with the tale of Usinara and the hawk and pigeon.

shots.B03C130S01H01: Lomasa names a long series of sacred places, from the Saraswati's hidden course and Vasistha's release at the Vipasa to Lopamudra's site, and ends by telling how Indra and Agni, as a hawk and a pigeon, came to test King Usinara.

B03C131.summary: Indra, in the form of a hawk, demands the pigeon that has sought King Usinara's protection, since hawks must eat pigeons. Usinara refuses to give up a suppliant and offers other food or any gift except the pigeon. When the hawk insists, Usinara cuts off his own flesh to match the pigeon's weight, and when the pigeon outweighs it, he climbs onto the scale himself; then Indra and Agni reveal themselves and promise him enduring glory.

scenes.B03C131S01: The hawk demands the pigeon, Usinara refuses to give it up, offers his own flesh in its place, and is then honoured by Indra and Agni.

shots.B03C131S01H01: The hawk demands the pigeon as food and argues that a king must not withhold it, while Usinara refuses to surrender a suppliant and offers other food or any gift except the pigeon.
shots.B03C131S01H02: Usinara offers to weigh his own flesh against the pigeon, and the hawk accepts the offer.
shots.B03C131S01H03: Usinara cuts off flesh to balance the pigeon, and when the pigeon outweighs it, he climbs onto the scale himself, having no flesh left.
shots.B03C131S01H04: Indra and Agni reveal themselves, promise Usinara lasting glory, and Usinara ascends to heaven, where holy sages and gods are seen at his old residence.

B03C132.summary: Lomasa points out the hermitage of Swetaketu, who received speech from the goddess Saraswati, and mentions his nephew Ashtavakra, who defeated Vandin in debate. Yudhishthira asks why Ashtavakra was born crooked and how he won that victory. Lomasa tells of Kahoda, who was cursed by his unborn son for faulty recitation, lost a debate to Vandin, and was drowned, and of Ashtavakra's journey to King Janaka's sacrifice.

scenes.B03C132S01: Lomasa introduces Swetaketu's hermitage and Ashtavakra's story, Yudhishthira asks about his deformity, and Lomasa explains the curse, Kahoda's drowning, and the journey to Janaka.

shots.B03C132S01H01: Lomasa points out the hermitage of Swetaketu, who received speech from Saraswati, and tells of Swetaketu's nephew Ashtavakra, who defeated Vandin in a contest.
shots.B03C132S01H02: Yudhishthira asks Lomasa how Ashtavakra came to be crooked in eight places and how he defeated Vandin.
shots.B03C132S01H03: Lomasa tells how Kahoda, a pupil of Uddalaka and husband of Sujata, was cursed in the womb for faulty recitation, lost a debate to Vandin and was drowned, how the family hid the truth from Ashtavakra until Swetaketu mocked him, and how the two then set out for Janaka's sacrifice.

B03C133.summary: At the gate of King Janaka's sacrifice, the boy Ashtavakra argues with the gatekeeper, who says that only learned elders may enter. Ashtavakra insists that learning, not age or grey hair, makes a man, and he challenges Vandin, answering Janaka's riddles with unexpected cleverness. Janaka, impressed, admits him and sends him in to face Vandin.

scenes.B03C133S01: Ashtavakra argues his way past the gatekeeper, answers Janaka's riddles, and is admitted to meet Vandin.

shots.B03C133S01H01: Ashtavakra claims his right of entry at Janaka's gate, debates the gatekeeper about age and learning, challenges Vandin, and answers the king's riddles with sharp replies.
shots.B03C133S01H02: Janaka, impressed, admits the boy as a learned man rather than a child, and sends him in to meet Vandin.

B03C134.summary: In Janaka's assembly Ashtavakra challenges Vandin, and the two trade numbered verses counting from one to thirteen until Vandin falters and Ashtavakra completes the last one. Ashtavakra then orders Vandin drowned, as Vandin had drowned other Brahmanas, but Vandin reveals that he is a son of Varuna, and Kahoda, Ashtavakra's father, returns from the sea. Ashtavakra's crooked limbs are straightened when he bathes in the river Samanga.

scenes.B03C134S01: Ashtavakra challenges Vandin, and the two trade numbered verses until Ashtavakra completes the last and wins the debate.
scenes.B03C134S02: Vandin is revealed as Varuna's son, Kahoda is restored, and Ashtavakra's crooked body is straightened in the Samanga.

shots.B03C134S01H01: Ashtavakra enters Janaka's assembly, challenges Vandin in boastful similes, and asks the king to bring Vandin before him.
shots.B03C134S01H02: Vandin and Ashtavakra take turns reciting verses that count from one up to thirteen, each naming things in the world by number.
shots.B03C134S01H03: When Vandin falters at thirteen, Ashtavakra completes the last verse, and the assembly erupts as the Brahmanas honour him.
shots.B03C134S01H04: Ashtavakra orders that Vandin be drowned as he drowned other Brahmanas, and Vandin answers that he is a son of Varuna and that his victims will return.
shots.B03C134S01H05: Ashtavakra declares that Vandin's false arguments have been defeated and calls on the assembly to judge, comparing Janaka's silence to a man stupefied by a fruit.
shots.B03C134S02H01: Janaka praises Ashtavakra and places Vandin at his disposal, but Ashtavakra insists that Vandin be drowned, and Vandin promises that Ashtavakra will see his lost father Kahoda.
shots.B03C134S02H02: Kahoda, now restored, praises his son's achievement, and Vandin praises Janaka's sacrifice as the Brahmanas rise.
shots.B03C134S02H03: Vandin enters the sea, Ashtavakra is honoured and goes home with his uncle, and at his father's word he bathes in the Samanga, where his crooked limbs are straightened; Lomasa then invites Yudhishthira to bathe there too.

B03C135.summary: Lomasa points out sacred sites along the Samanga, including the place where Indra was cleansed after slaying Vritra, and then tells how the sage Yavakri, son of Bharadwaja, sought Vedic learning through harsh penance. Indra first tries to dissuade him and then, disguised as an old Brahmana building a dam across the Ganga, makes him see the futility of his task, so Yavakri asks for boons instead. Bharadwaja warns his son that pride brings ruin, citing the tale of Medhavi, whose life depended on a mountain.

scenes.B03C135S01: Lomasa names the sacred sites, then tells how Yavakri sought Vedic learning by severe penance and how Indra tried to dissuade him.
scenes.B03C135S02: Indra grants Yavakri his boons, and Bharadwaja warns his son against pride, citing the fate of Medhavi.

shots.B03C135S01H01: Lomasa points out the Samanga, Kardamila, Vinasana and other holy sites, including where Indra was cleansed after slaying Vritra, and urges the brothers to bathe there.
shots.B03C135S01H02: Yudhishthira asks how Yavakri, son of Bharadwaja, attained Vedic learning and how he met his end.
shots.B03C135S01H03: Lomasa explains that Yavakri, grieved that his father was slighted while Raivya and his sons were honoured, undertook severe penance until Indra came and asked why.
shots.B03C135S01H04: Yavakri says he wants Vedic learning quickly through asceticism, and when Indra forbids it, he threatens to offer his own limbs to the fire unless his wish is granted.
shots.B03C135S01H05: Indra disguises himself as a feeble old Brahmana and tries to dam the Ganga with sand; Yavakri laughs at the task, and Indra points out the futility of Yavakri's own penance, so Yavakri asks for boons.
shots.B03C135S02H01: Indra grants Yavakri and his father the revelation of the Vedas and all the other boons Yavakri desires.
shots.B03C135S02H02: Yavakri tells his father of his gifts, and Bharadwaja warns that pride brings ruin, citing Medhavi, whose life was tied to a mountain and who perished when it was shattered; Yavakri promises caution but goes on insulting other sages.
